classification: Speculative worldbuilding artwork informed by materials culture. Not a forecast, engineering proposal, validated material claim, scientific reference, simulation result, or evidence of a real deployment.
designRule: Each image carries one dominant first-principles proof and no more than three required visible relationships. The ten-image sequence carries the complete material-to-regional causal chain.

systems.title: River-width separation loom
systems.materialPremise: Durable low-fouling ion-selective membranes remain mechanically useful as long flexible ribbons in moving freshwater.
systems.removedConstraint: Separation surface no longer has to be packed into a compact high-pressure plant.
systems.topologyChange: Replaceable membrane bands, service piers, and navigation channels form a distributed river machine.

shots.dominantProof: A selective membrane remains thin, flexible, edge-reinforced, and serviceable at very large width.
shots.cameraVisibleScene: On a wet service table, one broad dark-green membrane ribbon folds over a ceramic roller; its cut edge exposes multiple porous layers held by a continuous copper-gray clamp strip.
shots.camera: Close oblique material photograph; table and ribbon only; no horizon.

shots.dominantProof: A hinged ceramic comb lets a river-width ribbon be guided, isolated, and lifted without a pressure vessel.
shots.cameraVisibleScene: One membrane ribbon passes through a low white five-tooth ceramic comb with both hinged side arms open; the ribbon lifts clear at one edge while remaining captured at the other.
shots.camera: Eye-level mechanism close-up on a pier; comb occupies two-thirds of frame.

shots.dominantProof: The active separation surface becomes landscape-length while navigation remains open.
shots.cameraVisibleScene: Four independent dark membrane lanes extend from a low service pier far across a broad river, with equally broad open-water shipping corridors between them and no treatment building.
shots.camera: Compressed telephoto from pier; high horizon; sky under five percent.

shots.dominantProof: One membrane lane can be withdrawn while neighboring lanes continue operating.
shots.cameraVisibleScene: A stained ceramic drum winds one wet membrane ribbon onto the pier while two adjacent ribbons continue through their combs into the river.
shots.camera: Medium side view showing one withdrawn lane and two active lanes.

shots.dominantProof: Fouling is handled by sectional replacement rather than plant shutdown.
shots.cameraVisibleScene: A sediment-darkened membrane section lies accordion-folded on a wash cradle beside a clean replacement roll; matching edge clamps make the exchange relationship explicit.
shots.camera: Close maintenance-bay view; no river panorama.

shots.dominantProof: Water treatment labor becomes pier-based textile and membrane repair.
shots.cameraVisibleScene: Three workers at a long waist-high pier bench inspect an unrolled membrane edge using hand clamps and ceramic replacement teeth; wet gear and spares occupy open racks.
shots.camera: Documentary interior-under-canopy view; people communicate scale, not lifestyle.

shots.dominantProof: Public crossing and freight navigation coexist inside the treatment section.
shots.cameraVisibleScene: A low public footbridge crosses above two membrane lanes while a small work barge moves through the open channel between them; service access remains separated by simple rails.
shots.camera: Transverse view beneath bridge structure; sky excluded.

shots.cameraVisibleScene: Thin shore ice and frost coat a raised membrane comb; the flexible ribbon remains submerged beneath it while a heated joint band leaves one narrow wet line.
shots.camera: Close winter mechanism view; weather visible only as ice and residue.

shots.dominantProof: The river loom shares space with freight, intake, sediment, and ecological passage.

shots.camera: High oblique infrastructure view; ground and water fill frame.
